assumptions: The NL states there are twelve finite states but does not provide their exact state names or full original logical transition table, so descriptive state names and mutually exclusive guard partitions were synthesized from the described operating branches.
The low-SoC threshold other than the stated full-charge threshold 0.95 was not specified; SoC <= 0.2 was used as an initial modeling assumption for low SoC.

Capacity symbols Pgmax, Pd1max, Pd2max, and Pbatt_Pmax were declared because the NL references Pgmax/5, Pd1max/10, DG1/DG2, and battery dispatch, but not all capacity variable names were explicitly listed.

The generated model uses forced guard transitions as a state-selection mechanism so changing inputs can dynamically reselect the applicable dispatch state. No parse or semantic validation is claimed at this SL-1 stage.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
PL = 0 behavior is separately described; no RES case is represented as zero load and no renewable production.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows RES first and batteries when SoC is suitable.
Dispatch priority uses LNG before diesel units after RES and suitable battery support.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.

decisions.rationale: Pbatt_Pmax is an external capacity/input bound used to select dispatch states. The NL says the EMS reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not define internal update dynamics for Pbatt_Pmax. Adding a write would be a meaningless or invented plant/environment dynamic.

The guard variables PL, Pbatt_Pmax, Ppv, Pw, and SoC are NL-grounded external inputs or measured quantities. The state-selection transition is intentionally controlled by externally varying inputs, not by internal FSM writes.

The guard variables PL, Pbatt_Pmax, Pgmax, Ppv, Pw, and SoC are NL-grounded demand/resource/capacity inputs. No safe NL-grounded action exists to update these internally without inventing environment dynamics.

The guard variables PL, Pbatt_Pmax, Pgmax, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and eng3_Pmax are read as external operating-condition and capacity inputs. The warning is conservative for an input-reactive selector, and an internal write would violate NL fidelity.

The DG1/DG2 last-priority guard depends on external demand, renewable production, SoC, and generator capacity bounds. These are required NL inputs, so simplifying the guard or adding artificial writes would remove or distort required behavior.

The overload-illegal guard depends on external demand/resource/capacity inputs. The NL requires this extreme-demand branch; internal updates to make the guard variables appear written would be ungrounded.

The transition from ZeroLoad_RES_Spare to Battery_Assist is intentionally controlled by externally changing PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbatt_Pmax. The DSL should preserve this input-reactive dispatch selection.

The LNG_Battery_Cover selection guard reads NL-grounded external inputs and capacity bounds. There is no NL-grounded internal update for these variables, and a self-assignment or synthetic update is forbidden.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL edit made. Required dispatch states, variables, guard partitions, and cut-in/cut-out command actions are preserved unchanged because the warnings concern intentional external-input reads.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.
variable_role_summary.source: SD-4 diagnostic refs and generic NL external-input rationale

decisions.rationale: Pbatt_Pmax is an external capacity/input bound used to select dispatch states. The NL says the EMS reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not define internal update dynamics for Pbatt_Pmax. Adding a write would be a meaningless or invented plant/environment dynamic.

The guard variables PL, Pbatt_Pmax, Ppv, Pw, and SoC are NL-grounded external inputs or measured quantities. The state-selection transition is intentionally controlled by externally varying inputs, not by internal FSM writes.

The guard variables PL, Pbatt_Pmax, Pgmax, Ppv, Pw, and SoC are NL-grounded demand/resource/capacity inputs. No safe NL-grounded action exists to update these internally without inventing environment dynamics.

The guard variables PL, Pbatt_Pmax, Pgmax, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and eng3_Pmax are read as external operating-condition and capacity inputs. The warning is conservative for an input-reactive selector, and an internal write would violate NL fidelity.

The DG1/DG2 last-priority guard depends on external demand, renewable production, SoC, and generator capacity bounds. These are required NL inputs, so simplifying the guard or adding artificial writes would remove or distort required behavior.

The overload-illegal guard depends on external demand/resource/capacity inputs. The NL requires this extreme-demand branch; internal updates to make the guard variables appear written would be ungrounded.

The transition from ZeroLoad_RES_Spare to Battery_Assist is intentionally controlled by externally changing PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbatt_Pmax. The DSL should preserve this input-reactive dispatch selection.

The LNG_Battery_Cover selection guard reads NL-grounded external inputs and capacity bounds. There is no NL-grounded internal update for these variables, and a self-assignment or synthetic update is forbidden.
The LNG_DG3_Cover selection guard is driven by externally varying operating conditions and capacity inputs. Preserving those reads is necessary for the required dispatch priority logic.

The DG1_DG2_LastPriority guard uses external demand, renewable, SoC, and capacity inputs to model the required last-priority diesel dispatch. Editing it to silence the warning would risk losing required NL-grounded behavior.

repair_rationale: All selected diagnostics are conservative design warnings about variables that are intentionally modeled as external inputs or measured operating conditions.
The NL explicitly says the FSM reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not specify internal dynamics for those variables.
The forbidden edits prohibit inventing internal plant/environment dynamics or adding meaningless self-assignments merely to silence warnings.
Because every request would require an unsafe or ungrounded edit, all requests are rejected/waived and no repaired candidate is produced.

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: with default PL=0 and no RES, EMS should select the zero-load no-renewable branch rather than charging or spare modes.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_no_res_selection

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when PL=0, RES is available, and SoC is below 0.95, renewable production should charge the battery.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC boundary probe: when PL=0 and SoC is exactly 0.95, RES production should become spare power, not battery charge.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_spare_at_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES covers nonzero load and SoC is below 0.95, demand is served by RES and only surplus charges the battery.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC boundary probe: when RES covers nonzero load and SoC is exactly 0.95, surplus RES should be spare power.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_spare_at_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: with RES below demand, SoC above the low threshold, and deficit within battery capacity, battery alone should cover the deficit.
scenario_results.name: battery_assist_suitable_soc_deficit_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when suitable-SoC battery capacity is insufficient but LNG capacity can cover the remaining deficit, LNG cuts in before diesel units.
scenario_results.name: lng_battery_cover_after_battery_capacity

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC boundary probe: at SoC=0.2, LNG-covered operation should include the Pgmax/5 battery charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_low_soc_charge_margin_at_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start priority probe: with suitable SoC and deficit beyond battery plus LNG but within DG3 capacity, LNG and DG3 should cut in while DG1/DG2 remain out.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_cover_before_dg1_dg2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC diesel-margin probe: when LNG plus DG3 is insufficient at low SoC, DG1 branch should add the Pd1max/10 charge margin.
scenario_results.name: dg1_low_soc_pd1_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start priority probe: DG1/DG2 should be used only after RES, battery, LNG, and DG3 capacity are insufficient but total diesel capacity can still cover demand.
scenario_results.name: dg1_dg2_last_priority_high_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start extreme-demand probe: overload completion is illegal in practice, but if selected it should activate all thermal units and cover the remaining lack by battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: overload_illegal_extreme_demand_outputs

decisions.rationale: Pbatt_Pmax is an NL-grounded external capacity/input bound. The NL says the EMS reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not define an internal update for Pbatt_Pmax. Adding a write would invent plant/environment dynamics or be a meaningless self-assignment. This same rationale was already waived in the FixLog and no new evidence changes it.

The Battery_Assist selection guard reads PL, Pbatt_Pmax, Ppv, Pw, and SoC, all of which are external input or measured operating-condition variables grounded in the NL. The state selection is intentionally input-reactive, so adding internal writes would be ungrounded. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The LNG_Battery_Cover guard depends on external demand, RES production, battery capacity, SoC, and LNG capacity. These are required dispatch inputs, not internal FSM state. Simplifying the guard or writing these variables internally would distort the NL-required dispatch partition. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The LNG_DG3_Cover guard reads externally supplied demand/resource/capacity values including eng3_Pmax. The NL explicitly describes reading such capacity bounds. No NL-grounded internal update exists, and adding one would be unsafe. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The DG1_DG2_LastPriority guard implements the NL-required last-priority diesel dispatch using external demand, RES, SoC, and capacity inputs. Editing it to silence W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE would remove or falsify required behavior. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The Overload_Illegal guard is required by the NL for extreme demand exceeding RES and thermal resources. Its variables are external operating-condition and capacity inputs. Adding internal writes or simplifying the guard would violate required grounding. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The transition from ZeroLoad_RES_Spare to Battery_Assist is intentionally controlled by external changes in PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbatt_Pmax. The warning is conservative for an input-driven EMS selector, and no safe DSL edit is supported by the NL. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The transition to LNG_Battery_Cover reads NL-grounded external inputs and capacity bounds. Inventing internal updates to these variables would model plant/environment dynamics not stated in the requirements. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The repair rules explicitly forbid inventing internal plant/environment dynamics or adding meaningless self-assignments just to silence such warnings.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.
variable_role_summary.source: SD-4 diagnostic refs and generic NL external-input rationale

decisions.rationale: Pbatt_Pmax is an NL-grounded external capacity/input bound. The NL says the EMS reads demand, renewable contributions, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not define an internal update for Pbatt_Pmax. Adding a write would invent plant/environment dynamics or be a meaningless self-assignment. This same rationale was already waived in the FixLog and no new evidence changes it.

The Battery_Assist selection guard reads PL, Pbatt_Pmax, Ppv, Pw, and SoC, all of which are external input or measured operating-condition variables grounded in the NL. The state selection is intentionally input-reactive, so adding internal writes would be ungrounded. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The LNG_Battery_Cover guard depends on external demand, RES production, battery capacity, SoC, and LNG capacity. These are required dispatch inputs, not internal FSM state. Simplifying the guard or writing these variables internally would distort the NL-required dispatch partition. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The LNG_DG3_Cover guard reads externally supplied demand/resource/capacity values including eng3_Pmax. The NL explicitly describes reading such capacity bounds. No NL-grounded internal update exists, and adding one would be unsafe. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The DG1_DG2_LastPriority guard implements the NL-required last-priority diesel dispatch using external demand, RES, SoC, and capacity inputs. Editing it to silence W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE would remove or falsify required behavior. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The Overload_Illegal guard is required by the NL for extreme demand exceeding RES and thermal resources. Its variables are external operating-condition and capacity inputs. Adding internal writes or simplifying the guard would violate required grounding. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The transition from ZeroLoad_RES_Spare to Battery_Assist is intentionally controlled by external changes in PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbatt_Pmax. The warning is conservative for an input-driven EMS selector, and no safe DSL edit is supported by the NL. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The transition to LNG_Battery_Cover reads NL-grounded external inputs and capacity bounds. Inventing internal updates to these variables would model plant/environment dynamics not stated in the requirements. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The transition to LNG_DG3_Cover is driven by externally varying operating conditions and capacity values, including eng3_Pmax. These reads are necessary for the required dispatch-priority logic. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

The transition to DG1_DG2_LastPriority uses external demand, renewable production, SoC, and generator capacity bounds to encode the required last-priority diesel branch. Changing it solely to silence the warning would regress NL fidelity. This was already waived in the FixLog with no new evidence.

evidence.summary: The accepted SL-9 edit exactly addresses the hard simulation failure: with default inputs PL=0, Ppv=0, Pw=0, the guard partition corresponds to the zero-load/no-renewable branch, so changing the initial transition from ZeroLoad_RES_Charge to ZeroLoad_NoRES makes default initialization select the expected state instead of an RES charging state.

The DSL diff is minimal and localized: only the root initial transition target changed. All dispatch states, input variables PL/Ppv/Pw/SoC/capacity bounds, output variables Pgen_req/Pbatt_discharge/Pbatt_charge/Pspare, cut-in/cut-out command variables, forced state-selection guards, and enter actions remain textually preserved.

The NL requirements are not regressed by this edit. Zero-load RES charging and spare behavior remain available via forced guards when PL=0 and Ppv+Pw>0 with the appropriate SoC threshold, while PL=0 and no renewable production is now represented by the neutral ZeroLoad_NoRES branch. RES-covering, battery-assist, LNG-priority, low-SoC charge-margin, diesel last-priority, and overload-illegal branches are unchanged.

The FixLog shows earlier SD-4 design warnings about external input reads were already rejected/waived as conservative and non-hard; the current repair does not revisit or alter those waived issues. The current hard SD-6 simulation request was accepted by SL-9 and repaired with the smallest globally consistent edit.

The local SD-10 rejection reports missing_required_grounding for abstract/ID-level elements, but this is not evidence that the candidate dropped required behavior: the concrete DSL still contains the corresponding forced transitions to each listed dispatch state and the individual cutin_/cutout_ command variables implementing the abstract cutin_cutout_commands obligation.

local_override_rationale: Override the local_check_evidence rejection kind missing_required_grounding because the reported missing transition IDs are naming/grounding-label mismatches rather than absent DSL behavior. The DSL has concrete forced transitions `! * -> ZeroLoad_RES_Charge`, `! * -> ZeroLoad_RES_Spare`, `! * -> RES_Covers_Charge`, `! * -> RES_Covers_Spare`, `! * -> Battery_Assist`, `! * -> LNG_Battery_Cover`, `! * -> LNG_LowSoC_ChargeMargin`, `! * -> LNG_DG3_Cover`, `! * -> DG1_LowSoC_ChargeMargin`, `! * -> DG1_DG2_LastPriority`, and `! * -> Overload_Illegal`; they are simply not labeled with the grounding IDs `transition:select_*`.

Override the reported missing `variable:cutin_cutout_commands` because the NL requires issuing cut-in and cut-out commands, and the concrete DSL represents that obligation with individual command variables `cutin_LNG`, `cutout_LNG`, `cutin_DG3`, `cutout_DG3`, `cutin_DG1`, `cutout_DG1`, `cutin_DG2`, `cutout_DG2`, plus `load_cutout`. These variables and their state actions were preserved unchanged.

The local target_resolved=false is inconsistent with the actual repaired scenario: the only failing SD-6 scenario was default initialization at PL=0, Ppv=0, Pw=0, and the candidate now initializes directly into ZeroLoad_NoRES. The local rejection did not identify any semantic regression caused by the one-line initial-target edit.

The local drift_risk=major is conservative for grounding bookkeeping, not behavioral drift. The candidate changes one initial transition target and does not delete or weaken any NL-required state, guard, action, variable, or scenario obligation.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Change the root initial transition from ZeroLoad_RES_Charge to ZeroLoad_NoRES.']
decisions.rationale: The failure is caused by the unconditional initial transition entering ZeroLoad_RES_Charge even when default inputs are PL=0, Ppv=0, Pw=0. The smallest NL-consistent repair is to make the default initial leaf ZeroLoad_NoRES, which matches the default zero-load/no-renewable condition while preserving the existing forced guard-selection transitions for dynamic reselection on subsequent cycles.

diff_summary.summary: Changed only the initial transition inside LNGShipEMS from `[*] -> ZeroLoad_RES_Charge;` to `[*] -> ZeroLoad_NoRES;` so default zero-load/no-RES initialization selects the correct branch.

repair_rationale: Default-init execution enters the root initial target before any subsequent dynamic forced reselection can correct the branch.
With declared default inputs PL=0, Ppv=0, and Pw=0, the NL-grounded zero-load/no-renewable branch is ZeroLoad_NoRES.
All required dispatch states, variables, guard-selection transitions, output assignments, and cut-in/cut-out commands are preserved.

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: with default PL=0 and no RES, EMS should select the zero-load no-renewable branch rather than charging or spare modes.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_no_res_selection

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when PL=0, RES is available, and SoC is below 0.95, renewable production should charge the battery.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC boundary probe: when PL=0 and SoC is exactly 0.95, RES production should become spare power, not battery charge.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_spare_at_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES covers nonzero load and SoC is below 0.95, demand is served by RES and only surplus charges the battery.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start SoC boundary probe: when RES covers nonzero load and SoC is exactly 0.95, surplus RES should be spare power.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_spare_at_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: with RES below demand, SoC above the low threshold, and deficit within battery capacity, battery alone should cover the deficit.
scenario_results.name: battery_assist_suitable_soc_deficit_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when suitable-SoC battery capacity is insufficient but LNG capacity can cover the remaining deficit, LNG cuts in before diesel units.
scenario_results.name: lng_battery_cover_after_battery_capacity

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC boundary probe: at SoC=0.2, LNG-covered operation should include the Pgmax/5 battery charging margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_low_soc_charge_margin_at_threshold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start priority probe: with suitable SoC and deficit beyond battery plus LNG but within DG3 capacity, LNG and DG3 should cut in while DG1/DG2 remain out.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg3_cover_before_dg1_dg2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC diesel-margin probe: when LNG plus DG3 is insufficient at low SoC, DG1 branch should add the Pd1max/10 charge margin.
scenario_results.name: dg1_low_soc_pd1_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start priority probe: DG1/DG2 should be used only after RES, battery, LNG, and DG3 capacity are insufficient but total diesel capacity can still cover demand.
scenario_results.name: dg1_dg2_last_priority_high_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start extreme-demand probe: overload completion is illegal in practice, but if selected it should activate all thermal units and cover the remaining lack by battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: overload_illegal_extreme_demand_outputs

findings.summary: The model reduces dynamic EMS control to stateless guard-based dispatch selection, which is acceptable as a candidate partition but under-represents temporal controller dynamics.

evidence: NL says the overload completion state is illegal and shall never occur in practice, but if extreme demand exceeds all resources the EMS activates all thermal units and covers the lack by battery discharge.
DSL Overload_Illegal guard selects extreme demand beyond RES and thermal resources.
Overload_Illegal enter action sets all thermal cutin flags to 1 and computes Pbatt_discharge as the remaining lack.
The model does not add an unsupported load-shedding recovery action in this branch.
findings.summary: The overload branch is selectable, but its outputs align with the NL's specified illegal completion behavior; no blocking unsafe recovery was identified.
